subject: Burst-scaling mechanics & deal-led provisioning for CascadeIX
messages:
From: Anna Rios <anna@cascadeix.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Burst window for Q4 promo — capacity ask and SLA questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ramping up a targeted promotional push the week of Nov 9 and expect a short-lived, high-concurrency spike across inference endpoints (text generation + chat). We've attached a one-page summary of expected traffic and a rough RPS heatmap.

High-level ask: can Redwood support a deal that combines a small committed slab for baseline (for predictability) plus a predictable "burst uplift" for the promo window (48 hours) with clear rate caps and billing terms? Specifically:
- Baseline: 8 concurrent streams sustained, ~200k tokens/day
- Peak: up to 12x baseline RPS for ~6 hours/day over two days
- We need a fallback plan if dedicated capacity is saturated — preemptible or lower-tier model acceptable, but must preserve 99th %-ile latency targets for critical flows.

Please loop in ops/infra folks as needed; attached is our traffic extract (CIX_burst_request_20260929.pdf). Would like a short call this week to align on sizing and contractual language.

Best,
Anna
Anna Rios | Head of Platform, CascadeIX
anna@cascadeix.com

Attachments: CIX_burst_request_20260929.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Rios <anna@cascadeix.com>
Cc: stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-30T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Burst window for Q4 promo — capacity ask and SLA questions

Anna — thanks for the detail and the attachment. Putting a short proposal on the table so we can move quickly:

1) Provisioning model (deal-led):
- Committed baseline: a 8-slot dedicated pool (mixed T4/A10 equivalent) sized to meet your sustained 8 concurrent streams. This is priced as a monthly reserved slab.
- Transactional burst pool: a configurable ephemeral pool that can be hot-provisioned to ~96 concurrent-equivalent units (~12x baseline) for the promo window. Ephemeral pool is billed on usage (per-minute) with a published uplift multiplier for burst tokens.

2) Autoscale & guardrails:
- Activation: burst pool can be triggered by a Deal Action (scheduled window) or by policy threshold (e.g., sustained 3-min avg > 70% baseline).
- Headroom: start with a 20% headroom buffer on the baseline to absorb microbursts.
- Safe-fallback: when ephemeral capacity exhausted, auto-route non-critical traffic to a quantized model variant with preserved 95th %-ile latency; critical endpoints continue to use any remaining dedicated capacity.
- Burst cap: we can enforce a hard uplift cap (tokens/min) to limit billing surprises.

3) Operational runbook & timelines:
- Pre-warm: 6 hours pre-warm request to allocate ephemeral H100-backed nodes for peak 1.
- Monitoring: custom dashboard and a webhook to your ops channel; token-level billing visible via Console.
- Post-mortem: we provide a short usage summary and cost breakdown within 48 hours after window.

Attaching a preliminary capacity matrix (cix_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a draft clause we typically include in SOWs (burst-autoscale-draft-clauses.docx). Can Karthik and Ben jump in on the sizing specifics? If this sounds aligned, I'll propose a 30-min sync on Thu 10/1.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Attachments: cix_capacity_matrix_v1.xlsx, burst-autoscale-draft-clauses.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, Anna Rios <anna@cascadeix.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Burst window for Q4 promo — capacity ask and SLA questions

Quick technical readout and proposed fleet mix from infra:

- Baseline (8 concurrent streams): fit comfortably on 4 x A10G-equivalent instances (shared KV cache, 1x replica). This gives predictable throughput and low steady-state cost.
- Burst target (~12x baseline concurrency): suggest a staged ephemeral pool of up to 12 nodes with the following mix: 8 x A10G (fast warm capacity), 4 x H100 (for the short high-throughput windows). H100 is recommended only for the shortest, highest-parallel phases to avoid cost explosion.
- Autoscale kinetics: continuous batching / token-throttling combined with a token-rate cap. We recommend kinematic thresholds: scale-up when 95th %-tile latency > 300ms for 120s, scale-down after 180s of headroom.
- Pre-warm behavior: cold start for H100-backed workers is ~8–12 minutes; we'll keep warm placeholders if you require sub-3-minute ramp.
- Fallback routing: we can configure policy priorities: dedicated pool -> ephemeral A10G -> quantized model (lower memory, fast path). Model variants are pinned in the rollout config so behavior is deterministic.

Operational notes for contract: include a clear definition for "burst activation window", a billing uplift factor (example: x1.6 token multiplier for ephemeral burst usage), and an explicit cap to prevent unbounded spend. Priyom — suggest we include a signed pre-warm request form (one-time) in the SOW so legal/ops can approve scheduled activations.

Happy to talk through the matrix on the call.

– Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Anna Rios <anna@cascadeix.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-02T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Burst window for Q4 promo — capacity ask and SLA questions

Thanks — this is helpful and in line with what our infra team expected. A couple of quick items before the SOW:

- Please include a concrete example in the SOW that maps a 48-hour window to estimated token consumption and the resulting uplift cost (example scenario helps our finance review).
- We want explicit contract language that guarantees: (1) a pre-warm window option, (2) a hard burst-rate cap, and (3) a defined fallback path that keeps critical endpoints within 99th %-ile latency target.

We'll review the two attachments and confirm availability for Thu 10/1 11:00 PT — Anna + one ops engineer (ops@cascadeix.com). If that time works, please send a calendar invite and any pre-call notes for the ops engineer (we'll need the pre-warm checklist and runbook excerpts).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Anna
Anna Rios | Head of Platform, CascadeIX
anna@cascadeix.com
